subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I need to build a phoenix model using the SDK carefully, since I can't test the API directly. I'll keep it simple but visually appealing, relying mainly on parts, joints, chains, sweeps, and extrusions, while being cautious about exact function signatures for joints like parent and role options.

My plan is a standing phoenix roughly 1.2m tall, facing forward with spread wings and long tail feathers—built from a joint hierarchy covering hips, spine, neck, head, beak, legs with toes, wings with feather joints, and a tail with feather fans, all connected via parts using position, bone, and direction options to orient geometry correctly.

For limbs I'll write a segment helper that computes the midpoint and length between two points to build a tapered cylinder aimed along that direction, and for feathers I'll use flattened cone geometry scaled thin on one axis, translated so the base sits at the attachment point and oriented along the desired direction.

Since the orientation semantics for feathers are ambiguous without a defined up-axis, I'm deciding to sidestep the problem entirely by applying the rotation directly to the geometry itself before placing it, so the part only needs a position with no dependence on an external direction convention.

Working out the rotation math for each feather direction...

Confirming thin-vertical orientation, I'm shaping feathers as scaled cones to get a diamond cross-section, picking a flame-toned color palette for the body, beak, eyes, and legs, and now positioning the wing shoulders.

Still placing feather geometry...

Now I'm mirroring the wing across left and right using a sign flip, naming joints by side, and attaching primary feathers to the wrist bone and secondaries to the elbow bone. Then I'm building the body from scaled sphere primitives for the torso and chest, with rod segments forming the neck leading up to the head position.

Adding head details...

Now mapping out the leg joints: hip, knee, ankle, and foot positions, plus the thigh-shin-tarsus segments and toe placements with claws at the base of each foot.

For the tail, I'm placing three joints extending backward and downward, then fanning out seven long feathers from the base joint with the center feathers drooping longest while staying clear of the floor.

Now I'm laying out the neck and head joints running up and forward from the spine, placing the head sphere slightly offset, and setting up a reusable rod helper for building these segments.
